transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maria Chen, Ethan Park (Redwood); Amir Sayeed, Priya Nair, Tom Reynolds, Dana Ortiz (Larkwell)

[00:00] Maria Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining um I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll run through a quick intro and then dig into the on-prem air-gap details. Ethan and I from Redwood. Amir, Priya, Tom, Dana, thanks for time.
[00:12] Amir Sayeed: yeah thanks Maria, appreciate it. We are evaluating options for running an LLM inference platform fully air-gapped inside our datacenter. Main drivers are PHI data handling and regulator audits.
[00:25] Maria Chen: totally, that's exactly what Redwood Private is aimed at. Curious - first high level, are you looking for fully zero-egress forever, or a semi-airgapped model where we can push updates via approved appliance?
[00:40] Priya Nair: must be no outbound connectivity from the inference nodes. Any updates need to be staged through our change window and transfer devices. We also need signed images, chain of custody.
[00:52] Ethan Park: understood. We support both patterns - fully offline nodes with a signed image update process, or a controlled update appliance that brings packages into the airgapped network. Our images are signed and we can support customer KMS/HSM for signature verification.
[01:06] Tom Reynolds: practical question on hardware: what GPU types do you recommend? We're currently standardizing on A40s and a handful of A100 40GBs, but we have limited NVLINK in our racks. Also curious about NVMe sizing for kv cache, and if Redwood uses local NVMe or shared storage.
[01:25] Ethan Park: good q. For throughput-focused workloads A100 80 or 40 are common; A40 can work but you lose some perf on large models. We recommend local NVMe per node for KV cache - low latency matters. Typical baseline is 1-2 TB NVMe per model serving node depending on seq length. NVLINK helps multi-GPU models; if you don't have NVLINK we can run multi-replica shards or model parallel variants but it impacts latency.
[01:48] Amir Sayeed: and what about rack power and cooling? We have mixed rack densities and older PDUs. Do you have min power per node?
[01:58] Maria Chen: we'll share a hardware checklist - usually plan for 3-4kW per high-density rack if you go with multiple A100s. If you're using A40s it's a bit lower. Ethan can send a more detailed spec.
[02:10] Dana Ortiz: timeline: our compliance group wants everything in place by end of Q2 for an internal pilot. Is that realistic?
[02:18] Ethan Park: tight but doable - depends on procurement lead times for hardware and change windows. Pilot scope could be one or two racks with a subset of models. We'll need a week-long bench and a short on-site install/validation phase.
[02:30] Priya Nair: security stuff - SAML/SSO integration, RBAC, audit logs, and where keys live. We have a Thales HSM. Can Redwood integrate with external HSM for model encryption keys and signing?
[02:42] Ethan Park: yes - Redwood can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. We support PKCS#11 workflows and can store wrapping keys in HSM. For audit logs we produce detailed per-request logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM; for air-gapped setups we can ship a log collector that persists locally and can be exported via secure transfer.
[02:58] Priya Nair: who stores model weights? They need to remain on our storage. We can't pull from external repos.
[03:06] Maria Chen: models are deployed to your infra. We can provide a model bundle that you pull from an internal artifact repository. No outbound downloads required.
[03:15] Tom Reynolds: how do updates work? Monthly patching is required; we have strict CVE windows.
[03:21] Ethan Park: two patterns: 1) You pull signed release artifacts from a staging repo we provide and push into the airgapped environment; verification happens locally against your KMS. 2) We provide a sealed appliance (image + packages) that you import during approved maintenance windows. Both give you control over timing.
[03:38] Amir Sayeed: does the appliance require any call-home? Our security policy forbids call home.
[03:44] Maria Chen: no call-home required. The appliance is fully self-contained. We use signatures to ensure integrity but no outbound connectivity is necessary.
[03:52] Dana Ortiz: on the model side, we need support for quantized models - we are trying to reduce cost per token. Any constraints for quantized ops in airgapped mode?
[04:02] Ethan Park: quantization is supported; the runtime has quantized kernels and we can produce model variants optimized for INT8 or FP16 depending on accuracy tradeoffs. That all runs locally - no dependency on cloud libs. We'll note a small accuracy regression sometimes, so we recommend evals on your testset.
[04:18] Priya Nair: logging retention - we need 7 years for certain logs. Can Redwood handle long retention locally?
[04:24] Maria Chen: retention is configurable. For air-gapped customers we suggest exporting logs to your long-term storage like tape or cold object storage. We can integrate with your internal retention policies.
[04:34] Tom Reynolds: network ports - our security team only allows a couple of outbound ports for the management plane. What do you need?
[04:41] Ethan Park: for fully air-gapped nodes, zero outbound ports are fine. For management plane (if you choose semi-managed) we usually need HTTPS outbound on a specific management subnet - but that is optional. We'll provide exact port list.
[04:54] Amir Sayeed: regulatory question - do you have any customers in healthcare doing PHI workloads on on-prem? Any references or case studies?
[05:02] Maria Chen: yes, we've worked with a few healthcare customers on private deployments; we can share anonymized reference and a case study with contact permission. I'll include that in the security pack.
[05:12] Dana Ortiz: cost model - how does pricing for Private work? We need a pilot estimate and then a committed capacity model.
[05:19] Maria Chen: Private pricing is a combination of a platform license plus optional deployment services. For pilots we often do a short term license with a fixed fee and then move to a reserved capacity contract. We'll send an initial quote after we get your rack specs and desired throughput.
[05:34] [06:00] Ethan Park: technical follow-up: what's your typical request profile? Average tokens, peak concurrent requests, latency SLO?
[06:07] Tom Reynolds: average prompt maybe 400 tokens, peaks up to 2k tokens, and we need p95 latency under 800ms for most endpoints. Peak concurrency is 12-18 concurrent users hitting inference.
[06:20] Ethan Park: that helps. For 2k tokens with those concurrency numbers we likely recommend 2-3 large GPU nodes with local NVMe and batching configured; I'll run rough perf numbers.
[06:33] Priya Nair: on auditing - change control and chain of custody for images is mandatory. Can you describe your release signing workflow?
[06:41] Ethan Park: we sign releases with our private key; for air-gapped deployments we can provide the public verification key and optionally sign with customer key too. The release manifests include versioning and checksums. We can walk your auditors through it.
[06:54] Amir Sayeed: what about fallback and reliability - if a node fails, can traffic reroute to another model copy without egress?
[07:02] Maria Chen: yes, we support multi-replica deployments with local routing. Failover is internal to your network. No external dependencies needed.
[07:10] Dana Ortiz: any special operator training we need?
[07:14] Ethan Park: we offer a two-day on-site training for your ops team as part of the deployment services or remote sessions. We'll include that in the SOW if desired.
[07:23] [25:00] (discussion continues - pricing, SOW, legal contact info)
[25:05] Priya Nair: legal will want a clause about breach notification timelines; we need 24-hour notification. Is that acceptable?
[25:13] Maria Chen: that's negotiable in enterprise agreements - we can flag it for legal.
[25:20] Tom Reynolds: I'll pull together rack specs and allowed outbound ports and send them to Maria.
[25:26] Amir Sayeed: timeline reminder - internal pilot by end of Q2, prefer install week in mid-June.
[25:34] Maria Chen: noted; we'll align on procurement timelines. Ethan, you'll take the infra deep dive?
[25:38] Ethan Park: yep, I'll schedule that and prepare a perf estimate and the airgap update procedure doc.
[25:45] Maria Chen: ok quick recap and next steps: we'll send security + SOC2 pack, appliance image signing guide, hardware checklist; Ethan will run perf/cost estimates; Tom will send rack/hardware details; schedule infra deep-dive next week. Any other final questions?
[25:59] Dana Ortiz: none from product - thanks that was helpful.
[26:05] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[26:09] Maria Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll send the materials and follow up on next steps.

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors - e.g., NVLINK sometimes transcribed as N V link; PM names occasionally clipped; some timestamps approximate.)
